subtitle: Lesson 5 · Step 3 — See What the Query Is Actually Doing

eyebrow: The query from Lesson 4, Ctrl+M first
code:
SELECT InvoiceID, PatientID, ProviderID, InvoiceDate, Amount, Status
FROM dbo.Invoices
WHERE PatientID = @PatientID
ORDER BY InvoiceDate DESC;
caption: Turn on Include Actual Execution Plan before running this.

eyebrow: Three things to check, in order

steps.label: Cost %
steps.sub: Highest percentage is where time is going

steps.label: Arrow thickness
steps.sub: Thick arrow into a small result is a red flag

steps.label: Operator name
steps.sub: Scan vs. Seek tells you how data was retrieved

code:
SELECT
  |
Sort (ORDER BY InvoiceDate DESC)        <- thin arrow
  |
Clustered Index Scan on dbo.Invoices    <- ~90% cost
  (reads every row, filters PatientID after the fact)
caption: A query for one patient is scanning the entire table to find them.
